data.title: Singapore Stocks Rise As Bank Gains Lift STI
data.description:
Singapore shares closed higher on Sept 25, as gains in the three local banks helped the market rebound from the previous session’s decline despite continued concerns over elevated global bond yields and oil prices.

The benchmark Straits Times Index (STI) gained 0.48% to 5,710.65, ending the week on firmer ground.

Banking heavyweights provided the main support. OCBC led gains among the lenders, rising 1.3% to S$32.01, while DBS advanced 0.7% to S$78 and UOB added 0.2% to S$42.57.

The gains came as Asian markets remained relatively resilient despite a sharp sell-off in global bonds. Longer-dated US Treasury yields climbed to around two-decade highs, raising borrowing-cost and equity-valuation concerns, while Brent crude remained above US$100 a barrel despite easing during the session.

Sentiment also remained cautious amid inflation concerns and expectations that the US Federal Reserve could tighten monetary policy further.

Among individual counters, Frasers Centrepoint Trust was the weakest STI constituent, falling 1.4% to S$2.05. In the broader iEdge Singapore Next 50 Index, Boustead Singapore climbed 2.8% to S$1.86, while Top Glove fell 4.1% to S$0.235.

Market breadth remained negative despite the STI’s advance, with 275 decliners against 232 gainers. About 1.2 billion securities worth S$1.7 billion changed hands.

data.title: Wall Street Rises As Microsoft, AI Stocks Lift Tech Rally
data.description:
Wall Street closed higher on Sept 25 as gains in Microsoft and other artificial intelligence (AI)-linked technology stocks outweighed concerns over elevated oil prices and a fresh surge in US Treasury yields.

According to Reuters, the S&P 500 climbed 0.51% to 7,743.41, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.48% to 27,068.72. The Dow Jones Industrial Average outperformed with a 0.93% rise to 51,828.62.

Microsoft jumped 3.7% after unveiling new capabilities for its Copilot app, including a coding tool and an always-on AI agent, taking its year-to-date gain to 7%.

Qualcomm advanced 4%, Dell rose 5% and Akamai Technologies gained 3.2% following an US$11.6 billion cloud services deal with Anthropic. Meta Platforms, however, fell 3.3% after surging about 13% earlier in the week.

Seven of the S&P 500’s 11 sectors ended higher, led by information technology, up 0.91%, while industrials gained 0.6%.

For the week, the S&P 500 rose 1.2% and the Nasdaq added 2%, with the tech-heavy index having reached a record closing high on Sept 22.

Sentiment was also supported by reports that US and Iranian negotiators were exploring a phased path towards easing the conflict, including the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the potential lifting of Washington’s economic blockade.

However, pressure from bond markets remained. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield touched a fresh 19-year high before standing at 5.196%, up 3.4 basis points, while Brent crude remained above US$100 a barrel.

Markets are also increasingly pricing in tighter monetary policy, with traders assigning a 66% probability of at least a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate increase in October.

People Inc surged 11% following a report that MGM Resorts International was discussing a potential bid for the magazine publisher.

Trading volume remained relatively light at 14.9 billion shares, below the 20-session average of 16.8 billion shares.

data.title: Bursa Ends Flat As US Yield, West Asia Concerns Weigh
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia ended virtually flat on Sept 25 as concerns over rising US Treasury yields and escalating tensions in West Asia kept investors cautious.

At the closing bell, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slipped 0.69 point, or 0.04%, to 1,671.62 from its close of 1,672.31 on Sept 24. The benchmark index moved between 1,666.99 and 1,675.47 during the session.

Despite the marginal decline in the benchmark index, broader indices closed higher. The FBM 70 gained 90.10 points, or 0.51%, to 17,844.91, while the F4GBM rose 1.42 points, or 0.14%, to 1,010.47.

The FBM Emas added 15.37 points, or 0.12%, to 12,456.64, while the FBM Shariah advanced 14.51 points, or 0.12%, to 12,306.23.

AIMAX Bhd was the most actively traded counter, falling half a sen to 0.5 sen on 906.86 million shares after trading between 0.5 sen and 1.5 sen.

Zetrix AI Bhd was unchanged at 19 sen on 94.95 million shares, while Velesto Energy Bhd slipped one sen to 22 sen on 67.73 million shares.

Top Glove Corporation Bhd declined 2.5 sen to 75.5 sen on nearly 40 million shares, while Cypark Resources Bhd rose five sen to 82 sen on 37.33 million shares.

Trading volume expanded to 4.07 billion units worth RM2.69 billion compared to 3.32 billion units valued at RM2.74 billion on Sept 24.

data.title: Nestle Leads Bursa Losers As MPI Tops Gainers
data.description:
Nestle (M) Bhd led Bursa Malaysia’s decliners on Sept 25, while Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) topped the gainers as market breadth remained almost evenly split.

Decliners narrowly outpaced gainers 590 to 575, while 534 counters were unchanged. Another 1,224 counters were untraded and 43 suspended.

Nestle fell RM1.26 to RM90.20, making it the day’s biggest loser. Followed by United Plantations  Bhd, which dropped 52 sen to RM32.58, while Petronas Dagangan Bhd declined 50 sen to RM19.50.

Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd slipped 36 sen to RM30, while Sarawak Oil Palms Bhd lost 25 sen to RM5.73.

On the upside, MPI climbed 68 sen to RM44.18, leading the gainers. Batu Kawan Bhd advanced 50 sen to RM20.50, while Heineken Malaysia Bhd gained 38 sen to RM13.82. UWC Bhd rose 37 sen to RM6.88, while Hong Leong Industries Bhd added 30 sen to RM16.96.

Trading volume expanded to 4.07 billion units worth RM2.69 billion compared to 3.32 billion units valued at RM2.74 billion on Sept 24.

data.title: Asian Markets Split As Oil, Bond Yields Keep Investors On Edge
data.description:
Asian markets ended mixed on Sept 25 as investors grappled with elevated oil prices, surging global bond yields and lingering uncertainty over the Middle East conflict and US-China trade relations.

Tokyo bucked the cautious regional tone, closing 1.3% higher, while Hong Kong fell 1.3%. Sydney and Jakarta also declined, while markets in Shanghai, Taipei and Seoul were closed for holidays.

Oil prices provided some respite after their recent surge, with Brent crude easing about 0.8% after jumping more than 3% on Sept 24. However, concerns over supply disruptions and renewed inflationary pressure remained firmly in focus.

Bond markets added to investor unease. The benchmark US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level since 2007 on Sept 24, while the 30-year yield reached its highest since 2004. Japan’s 10-year government bond yield subsequently touched a fresh 30-year high on Sept 25.

Volatility is expected to remain elevated, particularly across commodities and bonds, while currency movements have been relatively moderate despite a preference for the US dollar.

Trade tensions also remained in the background after the US and China extended their trade truce by just two months to Jan 10.

The agreement leaves major issues including tariffs, agricultural purchases, rare earths and technology restrictions unresolved, keeping trade risks on investors’ radar.

European markets opened firmer, with London up 0.6%, while Frankfurt and Paris also advanced, offering a brighter start after Thursday’s broad global equity decline.

data.title: Gold Heads For Weekly Loss As Dollar And Fed Bets Weigh
data.description:
Gold prices edged lower on Friday and were heading for a weekly decline of more than 2% as a stronger US dollar, higher Treasury yields and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes weighed on bullion.

Spot gold fell 0.1% to US$4,274.90 an ounce as of 0632 GMT, while US gold futures edged 0.3% higher to US$4,310.30.

The dollar was on track for a weekly gain, making gold more expensive for holders of other currencies, while US Treasury yields continued to climb.

“When we start to see markets pricing in a much more hawkish Fed, it strengthens the dollar and is negative for gold,” said Kelvin Wong, senior market analyst at OANDA.

Expectations for higher US rates have strengthened after two Federal Reserve policymakers said further increases could be needed to bring inflation under control, following last week’s 25-basis-point rate hike.

Markets are currently pricing in a nearly 71% probability of another Fed rate increase in October, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

RHB Research also maintained a bearish technical view on COMEX gold after the metal extended its correction on Thursday, falling US$19.70 to close at US$4,265.10.

The contract opened at US$4,291.60 and reached a session high of US$4,304.50 before falling to US$4,246.40 and closing at US$4,265.10.

RHB said the lower close and a declining relative strength index indicated that bearish momentum was strengthening, while the 20-day simple moving average was also turning lower.

The research house expects gold to retrace towards US$4,150, with immediate resistance at US$4,400.

RHB advised traders to maintain short positions initiated at US$4,284.80 on Sept 23, with a stop-loss at US$4,500. It identified US$4,150 and US$4,000 as support levels, followed by US$4,400 and US$4,500 as resistance.

Despite gold’s traditional role as an inflation hedge, higher interest rates can reduce demand for the non-yielding asset by increasing the appeal of interest-bearing investments.

Meanwhile, gold demand in India picked up modestly during the week as the price correction attracted buyers ahead of the festive season.

Elsewhere, spot silver fell 0.2% to US$63.76 an ounce, while platinum gained 0.1% to US$1,750.80 and palladium dropped 1.5% to US$1,254.73. All three metals were also heading for weekly losses.

data.title: Stock Today: Top Glove Falls 1.9% Despite Glove Earnings Recovery
data.description:
Top Glove Corporation Bhd fell 1.92% to RM0.765 in afternoon trading on Friday, with 21.97 million shares changing hands as the glove maker came under pressure amid a cautious outlook for the sector.

The stock opened at RM0.780, climbed to an intraday high of RM0.800, then slipped to a low of RM0.760. Its last traded price was RM0.765, down 1.5 sen from Thursday’s close of RM0.780.

Selling pressure remained evident, with 3.50 million shares offered at RM0.770 compared with 1.06 million shares queued at RM0.765.

The weakness comes after RHB Research maintained its UNDERWEIGHT call on Malaysia’s glove sector despite stronger-than-expected second-quarter earnings and expectations of higher selling prices in October.

RHB said the earnings improvement was largely driven by higher selling prices implemented to offset rising raw material costs rather than stronger underlying demand.

The research house also highlighted persistent industry overcapacity and continued pricing pressure from Chinese manufacturers as key challenges for Malaysian glove makers.

Generic nitrile glove average selling prices had fallen to US$19 to US$20 per 1,000 pieces in September from US$27 to US$28 in May.

Malaysian manufacturers are planning to raise selling prices by US$2 to US$2.50 per carton in October, according to RHB’s industry checks, although most of the increase is expected to offset higher gas costs.

RHB said Chinese manufacturers continue to have a cost advantage due to cheaper coal and more secure nitrile latex supplies, giving them greater flexibility in pricing.

The research house noted that Top Glove, Supermax Corporation and Kossan Rubber Industries had delivered better-than-expected earnings in the latest reporting quarter.

However, it said several quarters of improved profitability would be needed before a sustained recovery could materially change valuations, with the industry’s excess capacity remaining a key structural issue.

data.title: Dollar Set For Second Straight Weekly Gain On Rate Bets
data.description:
The US dollar was on track for its first back-to-back weekly gain in more than three months on Friday as surging Treasury yields and growing expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes kept the greenback near multi-month highs.

The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of major currencies, has risen more than 1% this week to a two-month high, although it eased slightly to 101.2 in Asian trading.

The stronger dollar pushed the euro to a two-month low of US$1.1370, putting it on course for a third straight weekly decline. Sterling also remained near a three-month low of US$1.3220 and was headed for its weakest weekly performance in four months.

Markets have sharply repriced the US interest rate outlook since the Federal Reserve raised rates last week, with stronger economic data, fresh energy supply concerns and hawkish comments from Fed officials reinforcing expectations of further tightening.

A selloff in US government bonds has also supported the dollar, with longer-dated Treasury yields climbing to their highest levels in more than two decades.

“Whilst the dollar should get a bid from higher yields, there are still ongoing lingering concerns around the US fiscal position, the unpredictability of US policy making,” said Khoon Goh, head of Asia research at ANZ.

“I think that’s why the dollar has really struggled to continue to rally, even though yields continue to increase.”

Oil prices eased slightly on Friday but remained close to a one-week high after a Houthi missile attack on Saudi Arabia revived concerns over supply disruptions and added to inflation risks.

Yen Recovers On Intervention Warnings

The Japanese yen bucked the broader dollar strength, recovering more than 0.4% from a three-week low to 158.15 per US dollar.

The rebound came after Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said US President Donald Trump had raised concerns over yen weakness during a meeting with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi earlier this week.

Katayama said this reaffirmed the shared US-Japan stance behind their joint currency intervention in July. She added that she and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent would remain in close contact as Japanese authorities stepped up warnings over renewed yen weakness.

The yen was still heading for a second consecutive weekly decline, however, after markets viewed the Bank of Japan’s recent rate hike to a 31-year high and its latest guidance as insufficiently hawkish.

“The risk of additional interventions should also keep the upside in USD/JPY more limited,” Goldman Sachs analysts said in a note.

The bank also cut its 12-month USD/JPY forecast to 150 from 165.

The Australian dollar edged up to US$0.7018 while the New Zealand dollar was little changed at US$0.5659. The Reserve Bank of Australia is expected to raise rates by 25 basis points to 4.60% next week, which would be its final increase in the current tightening cycle.

The offshore yuan was steady at 6.715 per US dollar as markets assessed the outcome of a meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, where discussions covered AI, trade, Taiwan and the war with Iran.

Reuters

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Slips At Midday As Heavyweights Come Under Profit-Taking
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia remained slightly lower at midday on Sept 25 as profit-taking emerged in selected heavyweight counters, particularly industrial products, banking and telecommunications stocks, amid mixed regional and global market trends.

At 12.30 pm, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 1.14 points, or 0.07%, to 1,671.17 from its previous day’s closing of 1,672.31. The index moved between 1,668.81 and 1,675.47 during the morning session.

Elsewhere, the FBM 70 rose 85.44 points, or 0.48%, to 17,840.25, while the F4GBM gained 0.94 point, or 0.09%, to 1,009.99.

The FBM Emas advanced 12.13 points, or 0.1%, to 12,453.40, while the FBM Shariah added 21.09 points, or 0.17%, to 12,312.81.

Despite gains in the broader indices, market breadth remained negative, with 506 losers against 474 gainers. Another 503 counters were unchanged, 1,440 were untraded and 43 suspended.

Among the top losers, Nestle (M) Bhd fell RM1.42 to RM90.04, while Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd declined 36 sen to RM30.

Petronas Dagangan Bhd slipped 28 sen to RM19.72, Sarawak Oil Palms Bhd lost 27 sen to RM5.71, while United Plantations Bhd eased 26 sen to RM32.84.

On the positive side, Pekat Group Bhd climbed 29 sen to RM2.93. Batu Kawan Bhd, Southern Cable Group Bhd and Solarvest Holdings Bhd each gained 28 sen to RM20.28, RM2.87 and RM4.18 respectively. Rounding up the top gainers, Samaiden Group Bhd advanced 21 sen to RM2.90.

Meanwhile, AIMAX Bhd was the most actively traded counter, rising half a sen to 1.5 sen on 257.41 million shares, followed by Zetrix AI Bhd, which was unchanged at 19 sen on 50.53 million shares, while TWL Holdings Bhd was flat at 2.5 sen on 27.14 million shares.

Velesto Energy Bhd slipped one sen to 22 sen on 26.04 million shares, while Gamuda Bhd added one sen to RM4.85 on 24.42 million shares.

Turnover stood at 2.01 billion shares worth RM1.25 billion.

data.title: Stock Today: EcoWorld Gains 2.6% After Record RM5 Billion Sales Milestone
data.description:
Shares of Eco World Development Group Bhd (EcoWorld) rose 5 sen or 2.58% to RM1.99 at 11am on Friday, extending gains after the property developer surpassed RM5 billion in sales for the first time.

The counter opened at RM1.95, matching its intraday low, before climbing to RM1.99. Some 506,200 shares changed hands, with buying interest keeping the stock above its previous close of RM1.94.

The latest share price move came after EcoWorld reported that sales had reached approximately RM5.06 billion, exceeding its original FY2026 target of RM4 billion.

The milestone was driven by RM4.05 billion in sales recorded as at Aug 31, followed by a RM1.01 billion agreement with Tera Data Centers (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd.

The developer also reported a 20% year-on-year increase in third-quarter profit after tax to RM120.8 million, while nine-month profit rose 36% to RM424.3 million.

Revenue and gross profit for the quarter increased 28% and 19% respectively, with gross profit margin remaining healthy at 27.2%.

Residential properties contributed RM2.3 billion or 57% of sales as at Aug 31, while the Eco Townships division generated RM1.60 billion.

EcoWorld said future revenue stood at RM5.01 billion, providing visibility for earnings and cash flow as its projects progress.

The group also declared a third interim dividend of two sen per share, bringing total dividends declared for FY2026 to six sen.

data.title: Asian Markets Steady Despite Bond Rout And Higher Oil Prices
data.description:
Asian stocks held relatively steady on Friday despite a global bond selloff that pushed longer-dated US Treasury yields to multi-year highs, while easing oil prices offered some relief to inflation concerns.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was flat, with markets in mainland China, Taiwan and South Korea closed for holidays. Japan’s Nikkei rose 1% while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 1% and Australia’s resources-heavy index declined 0.6%.

The 10-year US Treasury yield rose 1 basis point to 5.1915% after climbing 20 basis points over two sessions to a 19-year high of 5.2251%. The 30-year yield also reached its highest level since 2004 at 5.5016%, pushing US mortgage rates to 7%.

Asian bond markets followed the selloff, with Japan’s 10-year government bond yield rising four basis points to 3.115%, its highest since 1996, while Australia’s 10-year yield also gained four basis points to 5.408%.

Investors are increasingly pricing further Federal Reserve rate increases, with futures implying a 71% chance of another hike next month, up from about 53% earlier this week. The dollar was heading for a 1% weekly gain at 101.25.

The renewed tightening expectations have also spread to other central banks. Norway’s Norges Bank raised rates on Thursday while Sweden’s Riksbank signalled a possible hike by year-end.

Oil prices meanwhile eased, with Brent crude falling 0.8% to US$105.75 a barrel after rising 3% overnight following a Houthi missile attack on Saudi Arabia.

Markets are also watching US-Iran discussions over a possible phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, which could ease pressure on global energy supplies.

data.title: KLCI Rises 0.1% With Oil Stocks Drawing Interest
data.description:
The FBM KLCI opened slightly higher on Friday despite a subdued session on Wall Street, with investors remaining cautious over elevated bond yields and oil prices.

The benchmark index rose 1.21 points or 0.07% to 1,673.52 at 9.15am after opening 2.56 points higher at 1,674.87.

Utilities and renewable energy counters led some of the early gains. Northern Solar jumped 9.32% to RM1.29, Solarvest gained 3.08% to RM4.02 and Tenaga Nasional rose 0.77% to RM13.16.

Hong Leong Financial Group added 10 sen to RM18.96, while PETRONAS Dagangan gained 10 sen to RM20.10 and Press Metal Aluminium rose three sen to RM7.49.

On the losing side, Nestlé fell 78 sen to RM90.68, Malaysian Pacific Industries dropped 28 sen to RM43.22 and Dutch Lady shed 26 sen to RM30.10. PETRONAS Chemicals declined 10 sen to RM4.48.

Wall Street provided little direction overnight. The S&P 500 slipped 0.02% to 7,704.13 points, while the Nasdaq edged up 0.01% to 26,939.37 points. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.31% to 51,349.98 points.

Malacca Securities expects the market to remain cautious amid elevated bond yields and oil prices, while seeing continued trading interest in upstream oil and gas counters.

It highlighted Hibiscus Petroleum, which produced about 32,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in July and has guided FY2027 sales of 10.7 million to 11.2 million barrels of oil equivalent.

Dayang Enterprise remained supported by an order book of more than RM4 billion, while Deleum has an order book of RM2.4 billion that provides earnings visibility.

data.title: Ringgit Gains Ground Against Dollar And Major Currencies
data.description:
The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and most major currencies on Friday, although global foreign exchange markets remained mixed.

At 8am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.0810/0865 against the greenback from Thursday’s close of 4.0840/0880.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said US Treasury yields remained an important influence on market sentiment, with the 30-year US Treasury yield rising eight basis points to 5.48%, its highest level in two decades.

“The rise in long-term bond yields implies that an inflation risk premium is building up, as heightened geopolitical risks in West Asia could exert upward pressure on crude oil prices.

“All this appears to have supported the US Dollar Index (DXY), which rose 0.19 per cent to 101.285 points, amid expectations that the US Federal Reserve will continue tightening monetary policy,” he told Bernama.

He expects the ringgit to trade between RM4.08 and RM4.10 against the US dollar today.

The local currency also strengthened against the euro to 4.6413/6476 from 4.6451/6497 previously and gained against the pound to 5.3910/3983 from 5.4023/4076.

Against the Japanese yen, the ringgit rose to 2.5694/5730 from 2.5723/5750.

The ringgit also advanced against several ASEAN currencies. It strengthened against the Singapore dollar to 3.1885/1931 from 3.1906/1940 and against the Thai baht to 12.1854/2091 from 12.1950/2121.

It edged higher against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.7/228.2 from 227.9/228.2 and gained against the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 from 6.51/6.52.

data.title: Singapore Stocks Nudge Higher After Institutional Flow Reversal
data.description:
Singapore shares opened slightly higher on Friday, with the Straits Times Index (STI) rising 8.36 points or 0.15% to 5,691.73 as of 9.09am.

Market breadth was mixed, with 86 advancers against 95 decliners. Trading volume stood at 88.07 million shares, worth S$170.22 million.

Among the blue chips, DBS Group Holdings was at S$77.83, United Overseas Bank at S$42.48 and Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation at S$31.79. Yangzijiang Shipbuilding Holdings traded at S$5.23, Singtel at S$4.24 and Singapore Exchange at S$22.47.

CSE Global was among the early gainers, rising 3 cents or 2.38% to S$1.29.

Real estate counters were mixed, with CapitaLand Ascendas REIT down 2 cents or 0.88% at S$2.26, while CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust traded at S$2.23. Frasers Logistics & Commercial Trust was at S$0.87, Frasers Centrepoint Trust at S$2.06 and Mapletree Logistics Trust at S$1.09.

The opening comes as recent SGX data showed signs of institutional buying returning to several Singapore-listed stocks after net outflows in the first half of 2026.

Yangzijiang Shipbuilding recorded S$219.09 million of net institutional inflows in the third quarter, reversing a S$39.52 million outflow in the first half and bringing its 2026 net institutional flow to S$179.57 million.

Keppel similarly recorded S$159.20 million of net institutional inflows in the third quarter, reversing a S$35.70 million first-half outflow and leaving it with S$123.50 million of net inflows for the year to Sept 22.

Thai Beverage also reversed more than 90% of its first-half institutional outflow, recording S$32.15 million of inflows in the third quarter and narrowing its 2026 net outflow to S$2.22 million.

Among smaller and mid-cap stocks, nine of around 40 counters tracked by SGX reversed first-half institutional outflows into net inflows in the third quarter. Real estate names accounted for several of the reversals, including City Developments, Centurion, Hiap Hoe and Ho Bee Land, alongside Elite UK REIT and Keppel DC REIT.

data.title: RHB Stays Bearish On HSIF With 24,400 In Focus
data.description:
RHB Research has maintained its bearish view on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), keeping its short position as the index extended its decline and remained below key moving averages.

HSIF fell 124 points on Thursday to close at 24,691 points after opening at 24,808 points. It climbed to an intraday high of 24,828 points before reversing sharply to a low of 24,610 points and closing with a bearish candlestick.

The index fell another 64 points in the evening session to last trade at 24,627 points.

RHB Research said the latest price action confirmed persistent downward momentum, with the 24,400-point level emerging as the next crucial support.

A decisive close below 24,400 points could trigger stronger selling pressure and reinforce the broader bearish structure, it said.

The research house also noted that the 50-day and 200-day simple moving averages remained overhead resistance, limiting the index’s upside.

RHB Research is maintaining the short position initiated at the close of Sept 17 at 24,572 points, with a stop-loss at 25,500 points.

The next support levels are at 24,400 and 24,000 points, while resistance is seen at 25,500 and 26,000 points.

data.title: Stock Picks: BM Greentech And HE Group
data.description:
RHB Research has picked BM Greentech Bhd and HE Group Bhd as technical stock picks, citing bullish breakouts and improving momentum that could drive further gains.

BM Greentech staged a bullish breakout on Thursday, closing above the RM1.70 resistance level with a positive candlestick formation.

RHB Research said the breakout could allow the stock to extend its upside towards RM1.85, followed by RM2.00. However, a fall below the RM1.55 support level would negate the bullish setup and trigger a correction.

HE Group has also shown signs of strengthening momentum after testing its immediate resistance with a bullish candlestick.

The stock has been forming higher highs alongside rising trading volume, which RHB said points to strong bullish momentum.

A break above the RM1.08 resistance could see HE Group extend its upward movement towards RM1.15, followed by RM1.25.

The bullish setup would be invalidated if the stock falls below the RM1.00 support level, potentially triggering a correction.

data.title: US Markets Subdued On Inflation Fears And Rising Bond Yields
data.description:
US stocks slid on Thursday as inflation fears and rising bond yields outweighed hopes for Middle East diplomacy and for the artificial intelligence boom to continue its run.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell by 0.2% while the S&P 500 declined by 0.4% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 0.8%. Markets remained subdued amid a sell-off in bonds and concerns about sticky inflation. On Wednesday, the benchmark 10-year yield hit its highest level since 2007 after a S&P economic barometer showed strong business growth, adding to inflation pressures.

President Trump’s meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, meanwhile, remains the key event to watch in markets on Thursday. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US and China agreed to extend their trade truce for two more months, ending Jan. 10, leaving artificial intelligence competition, the war in Iran, and critical minerals as the primary topics to be discussed. On Thursday, several top US tech CEOs will join the leaders for a dinner.

data.title: Bursa Ends Lower As Oil, Bond Yields Weigh On Sentiment
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia closed lower on Sept 24 as renewed oil-price gains and elevated global bond yields pressured investor sentiment, offsetting intermittent buying interest in selected counters.

At the closing bell, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 4.12 points to 1,672.31 from its Sept 23’s close of 1,676.43, after trading between 1,671.48 and 1,679.47.

The broader market was also weaker as the FBM 70 dropped 78.99 points to 17,754.81, while the F4GBM fell 3.02 points to 1,009.05. The FBM Emas declined 36.08 points to 12,441.27 and the FBM Shariah shed 28.50 points to 12,291.72.

An analyst attributed the weaker close to moderate selling pressure as higher oil prices and elevated global bond yields dampened risk appetite.

Meanwhile, Zetrix AI Bhd was the most actively traded counter, with 425.2 million shares changing hands. The stock gained half a sen to 19 sen after trading between 17 sen and 19.5 sen.

AIMAX Bhd was next with 166.87 million shares traded, closing unchanged at one sen.

NexG Bhd climbed 5.5 sen to 32 sen on 64.62 million shares, while VS Industry Bhd slipped 1.5 sen to 23.5 sen with 44.35 million shares traded.

Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd fell six sen to RM2.07 on 43.46 million shares.

Total market turnover rose to 3.32 billion units worth RM2.74 billion from 3.2 billion units valued at RM2.99 billion on Sept 23.

data.title: Chip Stocks Slide On Bursa As Nestlé Bucks Weak Market
data.description:
Technology-linked counters came under selling pressure on Bursa Malaysia on Sept 24, with Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI), MI Technovation Bhd, Unisem (M) Bhd and Pentamaster Corporation Bhd among the biggest decliners, while Nestlé (M) Bhd led the gainers.

Market breadth was firmly negative, with 677 losers outpacing 436 gainers. Another 542 counters were unchanged, 1,246 untraded and 27 suspended.

MPI topped the losers’ list after shedding RM1.08 to RM43.50, followed by Batu Kawan Bhd, which fell 54 sen to RM20, while MI Technovation dropped 32 sen to RM5.81. Unisem lost 24 sen to RM4.50, followed by Pentamaster, which declined 23 sen to RM5.18.

On the upside, Nestlé was the top gainer, jumping RM1.96 to RM91.46, followed by Ajinomoto (M) Bhd, which gained 38 sen to RM19.64, while Pekat Group Bhd advanced 24 sen to RM2.64.

Northern Solar Holdings Bhd rose 16 sen to RM1.18, while MISC Bhd added 15 sen to RM7.92.

Turnover increased to 3.32 billion units worth RM2.74 billion from 3.2 billion units valued at RM2.99 billion on Sept 23.
